STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of mixed leafy greens (looks like arugula/rocket) with a few bits of dried fruit or cranberry and thin shreds of carrot, in a white square bowl. Photographed from above, nearly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square bowl is roughly 20 cm across at its top edge. Treating it as a ~20 cm wide vessel: area ≈ 20 x 20 ≈ 400 cm² (inner usable area roughly 330 cm²). I use the inner area of ~330 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Mixed arugula/rocket leaves (dominant), a few dried cranberries (2-3 small pieces), a few thin orange carrot shreds.

STEP 4 - Area: Greens cover about 20% of the bowl area (~66 cm²). Dried cranberries ~0.5% (~2 cm²). Carrot shreds ~0.5% (~2 cm²). Total food coverage ~21%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Greens: 66 cm² x 3 cm height (loose pile) ≈ 200 ml. Cranberries: ~2 cm² x 0.5 cm ≈ 1 ml. Carrot: ~2 cm² x 0.3 cm ≈ 0.6 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Greens 200 ml x 0.15 g/ml ≈ 30 g. Dried cranberries ~1 ml x 0.6 ≈ 1 g (rounded to 2 g given visible pieces). Carrot ~0.6 ml x 0.6 ≈ 0.5 g (rounded to 1 g).

STEP 7 - Energy: Arugula ~25 kcal/100 g. Dried cranberries ~308 kcal/100 g (sweetened). Carrot ~41 kcal/100 g.
- Greens: 30 g x 0.25 = 7.5 kcal
- Cranberries: 2 g x 3.08 = 6 kcal
- Carrot: 1 g x 0.41 ≈ 0.4 kcal
Total ≈ 14 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small handful of loose greens in a large bowl, about 30-35 g and roughly 15 kcal, is plausible. The visible amount is small, so the estimate stays low.
